sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from a causal law with sharp flat-boundary assignment; only the observed law is available.
sampling_model.overlap: There is no treatment overlap at a fixed score. Nevertheless, the lower side-mass condition gives positive probability in every one-sided ball around each \(x\in B\), so \(x\) lies in the support of each restricted score law. Sharp assignment and consistency identify the observed conditional regression on side \(t\) with \(m_{t,P}\) almost everywhere there. The declared Lipschitz representative is continuous; two continuous representatives agreeing almost everywhere on a support agree at every support point, since a nonzero difference would persist on a neighborhood of positive restricted mass. Hence its one-sided limit identifies \(\theta_{t,P}(x)\), and differencing identifies \(\tau_P(x)\). This identification is setup, not the headline contribution.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: First-half scores determine a fully explicit finite grid and estimate masses and packing counts; total clipped second-half side averages estimate the traces. Neither \(\kappa\), the density, nor the profile class is estimated parametrically.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives a univariate pointwise minimax order under a regularly varying design density.
The paper studies pointwise smoothness adaptation for an inhomogeneous univariate design; its logarithmic lower bound concerns adaptation over smoothness, whereas L is fixed here.
The paper uses spatially normalized loss for univariate designs with finitely many density zeros.
The positive-density random-design supremum benchmark informs the regular endpoint only.
The submanifold-integral result assumes a design density bounded above and away from zero near the target submanifold.

The positive-density boundary class assumes a continuous density bounded away from zero, smoother conditional means, and finite moments of order 2+nu; only its conditionally sub-Gaussian overlap is comparable here.

The isotropic boundary result is stated on a continuous score-density class bounded above and away from zero near the boundary, so its upper theorem does not transfer to the larger vanishing-density class.

body.tldr: The first-half geometry admits a complete, tie-safe, same-radius result: the empirical packing count is sandwiched between the population packing profile at the same bandwidth, with the necessary \(1\vee J_P\) floor, and every map is Borel. The former second-half no-global-log claim is not certified by this comparison. The frozen class permits arbitrarily many sub-bandwidth exposed score components inside one packing cell, so a selected-interval maximal inequality needs an additional entropy-controlling law property or a different estimator. The normalized flat witnesses and banked endpoint lower bounds are unaffected.

project_justification.gap: Boundary regression with vanishing one-sided mass requires both a measurable estimate of macroscopic thin-site multiplicity and control of within-cell empirical-process complexity. The frozen packing profile controls the first quantity but, without an upper-mass or local-entropy condition, not the second.
project_justification.niche: The closed contribution of this solve unit is the exact same-radius, empty-profile-safe first-half comparison. It identifies precisely which geometric information the empirical count does and does not recover.
project_justification.fill: A source-labeled breakpoint arrangement and deterministic mesh produce a Borel representative preserving every first-half membership pattern within distance less than \(h/4\). Odd-even splitting then converts empirical \(h/2\)-separation into population \(h\)-separation without shrinking the radius. The outcome-risk claim is separated out because its proposed exposed-arc block-mass estimate does not follow from the declared law class.

body.related_work: Gaiffas (2005) studies univariate regularly varying designs and pointwise minimax behavior. Gaiffas (2007) studies pointwise adaptation over smoothness in an inhomogeneous univariate design; its logarithmic lower bound concerns smoothness adaptation, whereas the present Lipschitz constant \(L\) is fixed. Gaiffas (2009) treats univariate designs with finitely many density zeros under spatially normalized loss. These classes are neither included in nor supersets of the present bivariate side-mass class, so their theorems do not transfer directly. Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu assume a continuous score density bounded away from zero, smoother conditional means, and finite \(2+\nu\) moments. Only the conditionally sub-Gaussian overlap of that positive-density class is comparable with the regular subcase here; their upper results do not transfer to the larger vanishing-density class. Conversely, estimator-restricted lower bounds remain estimator-restricted. The same-radius empirical-packing lemma is proved directly and is not attributed to any of these results.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The same-radius packing lemma is uniform over the declared base laws and allows atoms and arbitrary Borel score distributions. That generality blocks the proposed selected-interval forest: individual membership paths may be consecutive while the union swept inside one \(h/2\)-cluster has mass arbitrarily larger than a member ball. A valid no-global-log oracle would need a derived replacement argument, a revised estimator that counts within-cell patterns, or an explicit law-side upper-mass/local-entropy condition. The regular-design same-estimator corollary is therefore not re-added in this round because its cited oracle premise has reopened.
body.honest_scope: This round closes the pure empirical-packing and measurability result, including breakpoint ties, the case \(u=1\), the same physical radius on both sides of the comparison, and the \(1\vee J_P\) floor. It deliberately removes confidence-tail, zero-count, fallback-risk, and isolated-rate assertions from that lemma. The causal trace remains identified from the observed law by side support and Lipschitz continuity. The population oracle theorem, endpoint upper-rate adaptation, and regular-design same-estimator rate require a separate valid selected-interval stochastic bound; they are not consequences of the proved packing comparison alone. The flat-law membership theorem and banked endpoint lower bounds are unchanged.
body.interpretation: At a fixed bandwidth, the first half can learn how many macroscopically separated thin boundary sites exist. It cannot, under the frozen law class alone, certify how many nearly tangent score components occur inside one such site. The distinction is immaterial for the normalized flat witnesses but material for a uniform theorem over every law in the base class.
